title.zh: 量子計算新紀元：Quantinuum Helios 如何以 98 個離子重寫規則
title.en: The Helios Breakthrough: How a 98-Qubit Trap Defies Classical Limits

summary.zh:
【總結】
量子計算領域迎來了一個里程碑式的時刻：Quantinuum 公司發布了名為 Helios 的 98 量子位元 trapped-ion（離子阱）處理器。這不僅僅是數量的增加，更是質的飛躍。Helios 採用了全新的 QCCD 架構，實現了所有量子位元之間的「全連接」，並達到了業界領先的操作保真度。這意味著它已經超越了經典電腦模擬的能力邊界，為未來容錯量子計算和實際應用鋪平了道路。

【研究問題】
過去幾十年，量子計算機面臨著一個兩難困境：要麼規模小但精度高，要麼規模大但噪音滿載。傳統的固定式量子位元架構在擴展時，往往伴隨著控制線路的混亂和操作精度的暴跌。研究者們迫切希望找到一種既能保持極高操作質量，又能像經典電腦一樣靈活調度資源的大規模量子架構。解決這個「規模與精度」的矛盾，是讓量子電腦從實驗室走向實用化的關鍵一步。

【研究方法】
Helios 的設計靈感來自經典電腦的馮·諾依曼架構，將「記憶體」、「總線」和「運算單元」物理分離。它使用 137Ba+ 離子作為量子位元，因為其可見光波長更容易操控且誤差更低。核心創新在於一個四向十字交叉點（X-junction），它允許離子在環形儲存器和運算區之間自由穿梭。配合實時編譯軟體，系統能動態決定量子位元的流向，並在運算同時進行冷卻，從而實現了高效的全連接操作和並行處理。

【結果】
Helios 展現了驚人的性能數據：單量子位元閾門誤差低至 2.5×10⁻⁵，雙量子位元閾門誤差為 7.9×10⁻⁴，狀態準備與測量誤差為 3.3×10⁻⁴。這些極低的誤差率使其能夠執行隨機電路採樣（RCS）任務，而該任務所需的經典模擬算力已超過目前最強超級電腦的極限。這證明了 Helios 不僅在規模上達標，更在質量上達到了「量子優勢」的門檻，為材料科學模擬和密碼學等應用提供了強大的基礎設施。
summary.en:
**Summary:**
The quantum computing landscape has witnessed a watershed moment with the unveiling of Quantinuum’s Helios, a 98-qubit trapped-ion processor. This is not merely a count increase but a qualitative leap. Utilizing a novel Quantum Charge-Coupled Device (QCCD) architecture, Helios achieves all-to-all connectivity and state-of-the-art gate fidelities. Crucially, it demonstrates computational complexity that surpasses the simulation capabilities of the world’s most powerful classical supercomputers, marking a definitive step toward practical, fault-tolerant quantum utility.

**Problem:**
For years, the field has grappled with a fundamental trade-off: high-fidelity quantum systems were small, while scalable systems suffered from overwhelming noise. Traditional stationary qubit architectures struggle to maintain precision as they grow, due to complex wiring and crosstalk. The critical gap was the lack of an architecture that could dynamically route qubits efficiently while preserving the ultra-low error rates necessary for useful computation. Solving this scalability-versus-fidelity dilemma is essential to transitioning quantum computers from experimental curiosities to industrial tools.

**Approach:**
Helios adopts a design philosophy mirroring classical von Neumann architecture, physically separating memory, data buses, and logic units. It employs 137Ba+ ions, which allow for more mature and stable visible-light laser control. The centerpiece is a four-way 'X' junction that connects a ring storage area to multiple operation zones. This allows qubits to be shuttled like cars on a track. Coupled with a real-time compilation runtime, the system dynamically maps virtual qubits to physical locations and parallelizes operations, such as cooling and sorting, ensuring continuous, high-speed processing without the bottlenecks of previous generations.

**Results:**
Helios delivers exceptional performance metrics: single-qubit gate infidelity of 2.5(1) × 10⁻⁵, two-qubit gate infidelity of 7.9(2) × 10⁻⁴, and SPAM error of 3.3(5) × 10⁻⁴. These low error rates enable the system to perform Random Circuit Sampling (RCS) tasks that would take classical supercomputers millions of years to simulate. This validation proves Helios operates in a regime inaccessible to classical physics, establishing a new benchmark for fidelity and complexity. It positions the technology as a viable platform for advancing materials science simulations and cryptographic protocols.

keyArticle.title: A 98-qubit trapped-ion quantum computer with all-to-all connectivity
